drafts.after: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He feeds his flock among the lilies. First principle: these two belong to each other. That is the language of God's binding promise. It is also the center of this song.

drafts.after: Love is strong as death. Jealousy is cruel as the grave. Its coals are coals of fire, a blazing flame. First principle: this love is as strong as death and the grave. The seal on the heart and on the arm marks God's binding promise, kept for one person alone.

drafts.after: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. Friends are invited to drink abundantly. First principle: he comes into his garden. He opens the feast to his friends. This is the supper language of the covenant meal — the meal of God's binding promise.

drafts.after: Many waters cannot quench love. A man can give everything in his house. It still cannot buy love. First principle: nothing can put love out. No money can buy it. The flood fails. The fortune fails. Revelation shows the marriage that follows this love.

drafts.after: Your love is better than wine. The smell of your ointments is better than all spices. First principle: this love is the measure of the marriage song. It is also the measure of the Messiah's joy. The Messiah is the promised King, Jesus. His joy is better wine still.
drafts.reason: 'Outsmells all spices' becomes a plain sentence that keeps the spices, and 'the Messiah's own better-wine joy' is unpacked into whole sentences. The Messiah is defined with the glossary wording, and no claim is added beyond the source's.
